deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW (my interpretation, based on consistency checks). The page is a numerical worked example of Gauss's pentagramma mirificum. It uses two plane representations: the gnomonic (central) projection onto the tangent plane at a point o, and the stereographic image drawn in the figure. Several numbers in the machine transcription do not satisfy the obvious relations. The corrected values below are reconstructed from those relations and from the positions in the drawing.

1. Outer pentagon in gnomonic projection. The first list, with corrections, gives the vertices at scale 1/9:
   - 𝔇/9 = 12+8i
   - ℭ/9 = -44/9+110/9 i
   - 𝔅/9 = -11
   - 𝔄/9 = -3-12i
   - 𝔈/9 = 12-6i
   The second list is 9 times these: 𝔇 = 108+72i, ℭ = -44+110i, 𝔅 = -99, 𝔄 = -27-108i, 𝔈 = 108-54i.
   Defining property (my verification): for every pair of non-adjacent vertices the real dot product is -10692. That is, 𝔄·ℭ = 𝔄·𝔇 = 𝔅·𝔇 = 𝔅·𝔈 = ℭ·𝔈 = -10692 = -r².
   Hence r = √10692 = 18√33 ≈ 103.40, as on the page; at scale 1/9 the constant is 132.
   This is the gnomonic image of a self-polar spherical pentagon on a sphere of radius r touching the plane at o. Each vertex is the pole of the opposite side: o𝔄 ⟂ ℭ𝔇, and |o𝔄|·dist(o, ℭ𝔇) = r², and so on. The drawing agrees: 𝔇𝔈 is the vertical line at x = 108, and the large circle has radius r.

2. Star points. Extending non-adjacent sides gives the five points of the star (my computation):
   - V_a = ℭ𝔇 ∩ 𝔈𝔄 = (18/13)(218+17i)
   - V_b = 𝔅ℭ ∩ 𝔇𝔈 = 18(6+23i)
   - V_c = 𝔄𝔅 ∩ ℭ𝔇 = (99/2)(-4+3i)
   - V_d = 𝔅ℭ ∩ 𝔈𝔄 = (9/2)(-41-38i)
   - V_e = 𝔇𝔈 ∩ 𝔄𝔅 = (27/2)(8-23i)
   Each V is the pole of a diagonal, so oV ⟂ that diagonal: oa ⟂ 𝔄ℭ, ob ⟂ 𝔅𝔈, oc ⟂ 𝔄𝔇, od ⟂ ℭ𝔈, oe ⟂ 𝔅𝔇. These are the perpendicularity statements the page lists; the transcription's labels look garbled.

3. Lowercase points a…e. These are the stereographic images, at scale r·tan(θ/2), of the star points. For a point V with gnomonic distance |V| = r·tanθ, the image z on the same ray has |z| = r(√(r²+|V|²) − r)/|V|. Equivalently |z|² + 2r²|z|/|V| = r².
   Writing V = (594/m)u with u a Gaussian integer, this becomes Gauss's form z = (18/|u|²)·u·(√(m²+33|u|²) − m):
   - a = 18/47813 (218+17i)(√1761870 − 429) ≈ 73.728+5.749i
   - b = 18/565 (6+23i)(√19734 − 33) = 20.545+78.754i
   - c = 18/25 (-4+3i)(√969 − 12) = -55.0908427+41.318132i
   - d = 18/3125 (-41-38i)(√120549 − 132) = -50.822-47.103i
   - e = 18/593 (8-23i)(√21505 − 44) = 24.926-71.662i
   These match the positions of a…e in the figure, after rotating it 180° at about 2.27 px per unit. The large circle of radius r is the stereographic image of the horizon (θ = 90°). The marks aa…ee on it are where the side circles cross it; the arcs drawn are the images of the great circles.

4. Side arcs of the pentagon. Lift the 1/9-scale points to 3-space as (x, y, √132). Then cos(side) = P·Q/(|P||Q|).
   - 𝔄𝔅: P·Q = 33+132 = 165 ("∝165"); |P|²|Q|² − 165² = 285·253 − 27225 = 44880 ("sin ∝ √44880"). So cot = √(165/272) and the arc is 52°5'12". Logs: log tan = 0.108541, log sin = 9.89704, log cos = 9.788495.
   - Second block (by my computation this is 𝔈𝔄): cos ∝ 28, sin ∝ √1686, hypotenuse √2470. Arc 55°42'33"; log sin 9.9170, log cos 9.75081.
   - Third block (this is 𝔇𝔈): cos ∝ 57, sin ∝ √3381, hypotenuse √6630. Arc 45°34'16".
   Check (mine): the tan² values are 𝔄𝔅 = 272/165, 𝔅ℭ ≈ 1.23789, ℭ𝔇 ≈ 2.54508, 𝔇𝔈 = 1127/1083, 𝔈𝔄 = 843/392. They satisfy Gauss's pentagramma relations 1+α = γδ (cyclically) and αβγδε = 3+Σα ≈ 11.6227.

Purpose: to produce an exact rational/quadratic-irrational model of the pentagramma mirificum and to draw it in stereographic projection.
errors: No genuine mathematical errors found; all checked values agree with exact computation to the precision given.
Minor rounding: the real part of a (reconstructed exact value 73.7277) should be checked against the image; the transcription shows 73.762.

The page's labelling of the side blocks ('𝔅ℭ', 'ℭ𝔇' in the transcription) does not match the computed values. The numbers belong to 𝔈𝔄 (55°42'33") and 𝔇𝔈 (45°34'16"). Either Gauss labelled differently or the transcription misreads.

results.what: Planar (gnomonic) model of a self-polar spherical pentagon with all non-adjacent dot products = -r² (r² = 10692), i.e. o is the 'orthocentre' with constant power
results.modern_name: Pentagramma mirificum; gnomonic image as orthocentric pentagon
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Pentagramma mirificum notes, Werke III, publ. 1876); Napier's rules earlier; later Coxeter

results.what: Star points as intersections of non-adjacent sides; each is the pole of a diagonal (oV ⟂ diagonal)
results.modern_name: Polarity in the self-polar pentagon / pentagram with right angles at the points

results.what: Conversion from gnomonic to stereographic radius r·tan(θ/2) via z = 18u(√(m²+33|u|²) − m)/|u|²
Side arcs from 3-D lifted vectors: cot(𝔄𝔅) = √(165/272) = 52°5'12", 𝔈𝔄 = 55°42'33", 𝔇𝔈 = 45°34'16"; tan² values satisfy 1+α = γδ and αβγδε = 3+Σα

deep.surprise_reason: The pentagramma mirificum and its gnomonic orthocentric property are well-known Gauss material. This page is a concrete numerical example with exact Gaussian-integer coordinates, plus a stereographic drawing. It is a nice unpublished worked example, not a new result.
